- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply downward correction by 2–5%.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.0) mid-period, model frequently fails to adjust downward; reduce forecast by 1–3% per negative sentiment day.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 75 for 3+ consecutive days, forecast should trend downward; if below 65, upward.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns negative after 10 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–4% per day.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to overfit recent highs; use 3–5 day moving average to smooth forecast.
